newsitem.title: USA: US Plains feedlot cattle market quiet - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains feedlot cattle market quiet - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets remained quiet late Thursday, with most showlists sold out after huge sales late Wednesday, feedlot sources said.
Sources said next week's cattle will be priced at $65.00 per cwt, up $1.00 from the bulk of this week's sales.

Packers took delivery Thursday of some cattle bought late Wednesday, with more shipments scheduled between now and Monday. Several feedlot managers said they were current on marketings, which was supported by the light weights of many of Wednesday's sales.

One Kansas feedlot sold near 3,500 head late Wednesday at $64.00, with the steers averaging about 1,150 lbs and heifers about 1,020. USDA reported Wednesday's heifer sales ranged from 990 to 1,150 lbs.

Overall, slaughter cattle weights have continued to run well under year-ago levels. USDA estimated average slaughter cattle weights the week ended Feb 8 at 1,164 lbs versus 1,166 the previous week and well below 1,182 lbs a year ago.
USDA reported 72,000 head traded in Kansas Wednesday, with most of the sales occuring after 1600 CST/2200 GMT. The week-to-date total for Kansas was 101,300 head.
In the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma, USDA reported 67,300 head traded bringing the weekly total to 121,700 head.
